title: SPR Auto Technologies Ltd - 544344 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: SPR Auto Technologies Q1 FY27: consolidated total income up 51% YoY and EBITDA up 27% YoY, with PAT up 9% after higher finance costs.
summary.overview: Management reported 51% YoY growth in consolidated total income and 27% YoY growth in consolidated EBITDA for Q1 FY27. Consolidated PBT rose 7% and PAT rose 9% YoY, with higher finance costs from the debt used to fund the automotive interiors and lighting (Antolin) acquisition. Management attributed a near-term margin squeeze to commodity cost pass-through lagging by about a quarter, which it said it expects to recover next quarter. Standalone legacy growth of about 12% trailed the industry, which management attributed to mix shifts and weak exports.

financial_highlights.value: INR 300 million (per investor presentation, as cited by analyst)

financial_highlights.metric: Powertrain-agnostic businesses share of consolidated total income

segments.name: Legacy engine components (standalone)
segments.commentary: Management said manufacturing growth in the industry was about 12-14% against company growth of over 16%, though the analyst cited ~12% standalone growth. Two-wheelers grew ~19-20%, passenger cars ~11%, CV and tractor ~7-8%, and other segments ~4-5% (per management). Exports were hit by the West Asia situation.

segments.name: Automotive interiors and lighting (Antolin)
segments.commentary: Margins improved from 7-8% to early-to-mid teens after synergies and fixed-cost cuts. Management said the segment won several new customer programs post-acquisition. Ex-Antolin consolidated topline growth was said to be over 16%.

segments.name: Electric motors and controllers (EMFI)
segments.commentary: Management said the business doubled turnover in FY26 after Coimbatore capacity commissioned by end-December 2025, and expects full-year benefit in FY27. Management declined to disclose capacity or market share.

segments.name: High precision injection molded components / plastics (Takahata, TGPEL)
segments.commentary: Management said the injection-molded business saw very significant growth in Q1 and that plastics revenue grew about 2x last year. Takahata phase-four expansion has started, with new business revenue expected from early next year; TGPEL second Noida plant is filling up.

segments.name: Non-auto components
segments.commentary: Management said non-auto (compressors, marine, defense, railways, snowmobiles, lawn mowers, medical, music keyboards) has grown 15-20% a year over four years, but did not disclose its share of revenue.

guidance_outlook: Management expects volume momentum after GST 2.0 to continue through FY27 across two-wheeler, passenger car, CV and tractor segments.
Commodity cost increases are passed to customers with a one-quarter lag; management hopes the gap normalises in the current quarter (Q2 FY27).
Finance costs are expected to be temporary and normalise as acquisition-related debt is repaid.
Management said export markets (US, Europe, Middle East, Turkey, Egypt) have not yet recovered and expects normalisation to take more time.
Management expects to recover the lost margin from commodity inflation and said it will not lose margin.
Management said it targets consolidated EBITDA margins in the high teens and aims for Antolin margins closer to mid-teens.
capex_capacity: Acquired the piston manufacturing plant and machinery from Sunbeam Lightweighting Solutions Ltd; completed in Q1 FY27, adding piston capacity.
Capacity expansion underway across plastics, EV motors and controllers, interiors and legacy pistons; management did not disclose capacity figures.
Takahata phase-four expansion started, building a new plant adjacent to the existing facility on five acres of additional land; new business revenue expected from early next year.
TGPEL: second Noida plant has full capacity available and is filling up.
EMFI: Coimbatore capacity commissioned around end-December 2025.
Legacy CAFE-compliant piston and ring coating technologies already available at Ghaziabad and Pathredi plants; management said products are under customer testing and validation.
Management said all the tested flex-fuel products up to E85 are ready, requiring different plating with capacity already available.
demand_pricing: Management said realisation may rise to some extent with newer CAFE-compliant technologies, which cost more; management said it is leading the competition on these.
Mix shift toward smaller vehicles post GST 2.0 lowered value realisation per piece, per management.
Management said commodity prices have started to fall from unprecedented levels, and it expects normalisation within the next quarter.
Standalone gross margin was around 56-57% in the past two quarters versus 59-61% historically; management attributed this to product mix and commodity impact.
Management said it has back-to-back pass-through arrangements with customers across legacy, plastics, motors and interiors, with a one-quarter lag.
Management said the Q1 wage hike, effective 1 April, had a small impact on employee cost percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone legacy growth (~12%) trail the industry growth of ~20% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said manufacturing growth was 12-14% versus company growth over 16%, and that exports were hit by the war situation, so manufacturing shifted toward OE customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone gross margin hold while EBITDA margin fell ~200 bps QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix of product, market, and volume effects, plus aftermarket lag in Q1 and the commodity pass-through lag.

qa_highlights.question: Is any price increase needed from OEMs to recover the commodity impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said back-to-back contracts exist with a one-quarter lag, so the increase for the prior quarter's average commodity price is recovered the following quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is net debt and what are the leverage thresholds?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated net debt was about INR 550 crore as of June; net debt to equity is 0.2x, and management said it will not cross 1x.

qa_highlights.question: How is the fundraise going to be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said funds are fungible and will be split across acquisitions, debt repayment and ongoing investments; no split was given. It said the fundraise is progressing as per target.

risks_watch: Commodity-cost pass-through lag: management expects normalisation in Q2 FY27, so the Q2 margin is a key check.
Export weakness in the US, Europe and Middle East, with no clear recovery timeline per management.
Finance cost burden from acquisition debt, which management said will normalise over time; watch the repayment schedule.
Standalone legacy growth trailing industry manufacturing growth in Q1.
Undisclosed segment breakup: management declined to give plastics, Antolin and EMFI revenue and EBITDA for the quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, integration and margin recovery, but evasive on specifics: management declined to give segment splits, EMFI capacity, market share, non-auto revenue share and the wage-cost impact. On exports, it was candid that recovery is slow.
key_quotes: As far as fundraise is concerned, I think we are progressing as per target.
We are not going to lose on our margins.
So, we have outgrown the industry even as we speak.
At present it is only 0.2x. So, we don't see any reason why we have to even go up to 1x.
I'd really request all of you to reach out to our secretarial department for the questions so that we can answer back one on one.
